parentMoonshot.sourceClaim: Instead of programming machines, program cause-and-effect chains. Give it an end state and it discovers the minimum chain of interventions that would make that state emerge across physical, biological, economic, and computational systems.

narrowClaim: For known deterministic acyclic Boolean structural causal models, backward causal relevance pruning can preserve the globally minimum intervention cardinality while reducing exhaustive intervention evaluations relative to searching all controllable variables.

model.substrate: deterministic acyclic Boolean structural causal models
model.interventions: do-style overrides on declared controllable Boolean input nodes
model.objective: satisfy declared Boolean target assignments with minimum intervention cardinality
model.candidateCompiler: restrict intervention search to controllable ancestors of target nodes
model.comparator: exhaustive search over all controllable nodes
model.tieRule: minimum cardinality first, then lexicographic intervention variable set and assignment

benchmark.negativeControl: cases with zero distractor controls, where pruning should not manufacture a gain
benchmark.impossibleControl: constant target with no controllable ancestors and unreachable desired state

falsifier: Any benchmark case changes minimum intervention cardinality versus exhaustive search.
Any satisfiable case is called unsatisfiable or vice versa.
Median evaluation reduction on distractor cases is below 10x.
Negative-control cases show a manufactured gain larger than 5%.
Target or held-out outcome information is used to mutate the pruning rule after result execution.
promotionBoundary: A pass may support SOFTWARE_DEMONSTRATED for the narrow known-SCM intervention-pruning primitive only. It does not establish the full founder moonshot.
